title: Finite scalar local models under the normalized integral section comparison
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension in the scheme universe, and $X$ a Noetherian scheme [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Write $B_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ for the actual continuous integral coefficient ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For any ordinary $B_X$-module sheaf $M$, being constructible with finite constant scalar local models [sk-def-sfb-constructible] is equivalent to the following property of its image under the fixed exact functor: first apply integralSectionFunctor [det-prop-integral-criterion-reductions], then restrict scalars along integralDetailedCoefficientComparison.hom [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. That image satisfies IsIntegralStratifiedFinitelyPresented for pbcIntegralDatum: after a finite constructible locally closed stratification there is a pro-etale covering sieve on each stratum, and on each member the module is isomorphic to the restriction of the completed constant realization of a finitely presented module over PbcIntegralRing. The same finite stratification can be used in both directions. No bounded derived object, finite dimension bound, invertibility assumption, Tor bound or completeness assertion is involved.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10; Proposition 6.8.11(3), coefficient-presentation comparison in step 7 of lem-sfb-integral-constructible-completion-bridge. This is the heart-level scalar-model comparison, with no derived completeness assertion.

proof.text: On a Noetherian X, compactness and quasi-separatedness select the finite-stratification branch. Keep its same stratification in both directions. Convert a cover to its generated covering sieve. For any member factoring through a cover arrow, pull its point-model isomorphism back and use the existing point-pullback composition comparison. Conversely choose a covering presieve inside a covering sieve, push its arrows to the base scheme through the terminal-object isomorphism, and restrict to a universe-u small subfamily. This gives the original cover convention.

For every sieve member, use the global scalar-model theorem to replace its finitely presented point module P by N and its global completed constant realization. Use local-isomorphism transport to move its actual local isomorphism to the slice, then compose with the restriction of the global model comparison. In the reverse direction choose P for the scalar N, compose with the inverse global model comparison on the slice, reflect the local isomorphism, and cancel the point-pullback comparison. Retain the sieve, finite-presentation proofs, and stratification. These Lean constructions prove both implications.

lean.statement: theorem integralSectionLocalModels (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (M : AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) : IsConstantModelConstructible (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X M ↔ Scheme.IsIntegralStratifiedFinitelyPresented X (Scheme.pbcIntegralDatum l E) ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u + 1} (Scheme.integralDetailedCoefficientComparison X l E).hom).obj ((integralSectionFunctor l E X).obj M))
